blocks.content: kubectl logs shows what a container has printed to standard output and standard error, the fastest way to see what an application actually said.
logs retrieves everything a container has printed since it started, exactly the same captured output covered for docker logs throughout the Docker course, just retrieved through kubectl instead.

blocks.alt: Everything a container has printed, retrieved directly

blocks.content: -f follows output live, --previous retrieves logs from a crashed instance before it restarted, and -c picks a specific container in a multi-container Pod, the three flags that cover the large majority of real usage.

blocks.alt: Three flags covering the large majority of how this command actually gets used

blocks.content:
kubectl logs -f my-app-7d9f8c-x2k4p
kubectl logs --previous my-app-7d9f8c-x2k4p
kubectl logs my-app-7d9f8c-x2k4p -c sidecar
